title: Tiered LTS Upgrade Notice & Migration Playbook for runtime-1.20
creator: Ethan Morales
description: Purpose: Create a customer-facing, tiered communication plan and step-by-step migration playbook for the runtime-1.20 LTS channel. The deliverable will include: (1) short-form release notes for product and engineering users, (2) an admin-facing migration playbook with rollback/fallback instructions, (3) three email/portal templates tailored to: self-serve devs, enterprise platform admins, and Dedicated/Private customers, (4) a staged rollout schedule tied to rollout gates and automated upgrade tooling, and (5) update-to-FAQ and KB article drafts. Goals: reduce upgrade friction, minimize support tickets during the first 30 days of the LTS rollout, and give platform teams clear rollback/runbook steps that avoid capacity churn. Scope: customer communications, migration steps, risk/rollback playbooks, automated upgrade CLI examples, links to PRs and monitoring dashboards. Out of scope: engineering implementation of the upgrade pipeline itself (ENG owns that) and internal-only release comms (handled by PM comms team).
acceptance_criteria: One-page executive summary (<= 300 words) that can be used by CSMs and AEs
Three distinct email/portal templates (Dev, Admin, Enterprise) complete and approved
Migration playbook with explicit pre-checks, migration steps, post-validation checks, and rollback steps
KB article and Quickstart guide published to docs.redwood.ai with links included
Automated CLI snippet that performs dry-run upgrade and reports compatibility warnings (example command included)
Stakeholder sign-off from Eng Release Lead (Rafael Park) and Security (Anika Shah)

migration_steps: Pre-upgrade checklist: collect cluster metadata, confirm model variants pinned, take KV cache snapshot (script link in Confluence)
Staged upgrade: apply to 5% of traffic using rollout policy 'lts-canary-1' for 24h, monitor latency/error budget on dashboard
Full upgrade: escalate canary to 50% for 12h, then 100% if no regressions; abort if error budget > 2% or P50 latency regression > 30ms
Post-upgrade validation: run sample prompts from customer's regression suite and compare embeddings/tokenization diffs; file issues if semantic drift detected
Rollback: set runtime pin back to previous LTS version and trigger cache-backfill script; notify customers within 15 minutes via configured webhook
comm_templates:
Developer (short form): Subject: runtime-1.20 LTS available — compatibility notes
Body: Hi <name>, runtime-1.20 is now available in the LTS channel. Highlights: improved batching, KV cache change (requires migration flag), and smaller tail latency. If you use pinned model versions nothing changes. Run './rwd-upgrade --dry-run' to check your apps. Link to migration playbook.

Admin (detailed): Subject: Action required: Schedule upgrade to runtime-1.20 LTS
Body: Hello platform admin, we are opening the LTS channel for runtime-1.20. Please review the attached migration playbook for pre-checks, rollout schedule, and rollback steps. Recommended window: 2–4 hours. If you rely on legacy KV cache, enable --kv-compat and follow the automated migration tool guide. Contact CSM or support@redwood.ai for help.

Enterprise / Dedicated: Subject: Planned LTS rollout & required coordination for runtime-1.20
Body: Dear customer, we are planning a coordinated rollout for runtime-1.20 LTS between Feb 20–28. This message includes a pre-upgrade readiness checklist, an opt-out form for scheduling, and a support escalation contact. Private deployments will require a maintenance window with your infra team. See the runbook and open the case if you need assistance.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: KV cache format change may cause subtle tokenization/embedding differences. Mitigation: compatibility flag, dry-run scans, and post-upgrade regression suite.

Risk: Rollout automation could overload control plane if executed across many Dedicated clusters simultaneously. Mitigation: rate-limited rollout runs and a 'guardrail' script that enforces concurrency limits.
Risk: Customers on older quantized model variants may see minor quality regressions. Mitigation: include recommended model pins and rollback instructions in playbook.
